item.title: Glutton Kiran to Sage Kedi
item.description:
01: A Midnight Birth in Mumbai

I was born at 1:00 AM on July 2, 1989, at Rajawadi Hospital in Ghatkopar. My ancestral home was in Aswalwadi 32, Shirala, Sangli. A few days later, we moved to the village to live there.

My parents had an inter-caste love marriage, because of which they had to listen to taunts from family members every day. There was an atmosphere of unrest in the house. My father started committing domestic violence against my mother, and my aunt (father’s sister) played an equal role in it. Whenever I tried to protect my mother, my aunt would push me away and stop me.

item.title: My First Pilgrimage: A 5,000 KM Journey Across India
item.description:
From Civilisation to Temples

In 2016, I wanted to ride a bike across the whole of India to closely observe Indian culture and civilization. I would travel from one city to another only on my bike. My first long bike journey was in 2016, from Mumbai to Chennai. My second-longest journey was in 2017, from Mumbai to Delhi and back to Mumbai. My third was in April 2021, from Mumbai to Kolkata, and my fourth began on 2 May 2021, from Mumbai to Delhi and then to New Jalpaiguri.

item.title: The Vrindavan Journey: In Search of Devotion
item.description:
The Decision to Learn Devotion

On June 18, 2023, I decided to deepen my spiritual journey by learning about devotional practice, and the next day, I began my journey to Vrindavan. I had already visited Rishikesh to study meditation practice and travelled to Kamakhya in 2021 to study tantra practice, so this time I felt it was the right moment to go to Vrindavan and learn about devotion.

I shared my plan with my mother. “Like last year, I want to go to Vrindavan again—this time dressed as a sadhu—to immerse myself in devotion practice.” My mother already knew my pattern. Whenever I planned a 10–15-day religious journey, I would usually return home after just 7–8 days, abandon the journey midway, and restart it later.
